payload.one_line: Parses argv into operands/unknown and produces typed option and command-argument values per command.
payload.covers: argv intake, option scanning, value-source precedence, environment and implied options, argument coercion, mandatory/conflict checks, and parser regression contracts.
payload.excludes: Help formatting, executable subcommand launching, lifecycle hook ordering, and the derived TypeScript declaration surface.

flows.name: argv to typed options
flows.description: Normalize user argv, scan flags, coerce values, apply env/implied precedence, and validate the leaf command.

steps.what_happens: parse and _prepareUserArgs normalize argv before _parseCommand scans it.
parseOptions emits option events and addOption listeners apply parseArg, variadic collection, and source tracking.
Option and DualOptions define flag syntax and dual-option value resolution.
Argument defines required, optional, variadic, choice, default, and parseArg behavior.
Regression tests pin operands, unknown tokens, --, short bundles, and long equals parsing.

touchpoints.symbol: Options taking varying numbers of option-arguments
touchpoints.role: Documents parsing invariants and ambiguity controls.
Encodes command-argument syntax and processing hooks.
Owns the argv to validated values pipeline and scanner-to-value event boundary.
Provides stable typed errors for parser failures.
Encapsulates flag syntax, value coercion hooks, variadic values, and dual-option disambiguation.
Locks scanner behavior and ambiguity rules.

invariants.rule: parseOptions emits option events and addOption listeners are the value-writing path for CLI and environment sources.
invariants.why: Keeps scanning separate from coercion, variadic collection, and source tracking.

invariants.rule: Environment values do not overwrite CLI values and only fill permitted lower-priority sources.
The -- token ends option parsing and preserves the remaining tail as operands.
invariants.why: Supports literal arguments and documented POSIX behavior.

invariants.rule: Optional option values do not consume a following token that looks like another option unless it is recognized as a negative number.
invariants.why: Prevents one flag from stealing another flag's token.

pitfalls.risk: Negative command arguments in a non-leaf command are treated as unknown options.
pitfalls.consequence: Valid-looking negative values can produce commander.unknownOption errors.

pitfalls.risk: Short flag bundles such as -db can consume b as d's value under the default combination rule.
pitfalls.consequence: The intended boolean b option is silently absent.

entry_questions: Does a new flag string interact with short bundles, optional values, or negative-number detection?
Does it preserve -- and unknown-tail behavior?
Does the change alter default/config/env/cli/implied precedence?
validation_commands: update typings/index.d.ts and typings/index.test-d.ts when public API changes
